findings.source: RollupCore.sol:584 genesisAssertionHash(); AssertionStateLib.hash: keccak256(abi.encode(state)) with GlobalState { bytes32[2] bytes32Vals; uint64[2] u64Vals }
findings.issue: The ABI decoding and encoding of every uint64[2] are loops with a constant trip count of 2 (bounds 324..388 step 32, 0..2 step 1) that stay as whiles (33 of the 40 whiles), so their effect is never folded: genesisAssertionHash, a constant, still hashes mem[512 len 64], which the loop fills with zeros.
findings.rule: When the induction variable starts at a constant, steps by a constant and is compared with a constant bound, the trip count is constant; unroll such loops when the count is small (<= 4) and fold the resulting copies (here mem[512 len 64] = Bytes(64, 0)).

notes: All 70 ABI functions compared; forceCreateAssertion (554 lines) and initialize (369 lines) by structure (decoding, checks, storage writes, events, calls), the rest in full. No semantic error found (EnumerableSet add/remove in setValidator, the UUPS rollback branch without Upgraded event, decreaseBaseStake's pending-count logic all match). Loops: the three source loops (decreaseBaseStake over stakers, forceRefundStaker, setValidator) are readable whiles. The other 37 whiles are implicit: 33 constant-count uint64[2] decode/encode loops (finding), getValidators' storage-to-memory copy (P7), and 3 calldata-array encodings for the StakersForceRefunded / ValidatorsSet events. P13: the staker map is named isStaked (latestStakedAssertion read as isStaked[a].field_256); the EnumerableSet index mapping is named isValidator.
summary: Faithful on the paths checked with the three source loops readable; cluttered by 33 un-unrolled two-iteration uint64[2] loops and by raw-memory reverts/events/hashes inside decreaseBaseStake's loop.
